column1: # coercion_surface_sites.tsv -- THE DECLARED COERCION SURFACE (hq_T, R-662, 2026-09-13).
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A new descriptor tag owes an arm in every function that switches on a descriptor's
# tag, and before this census nobody could say what that set IS. The DT_BOOL tag (R-654) leaked three
# times in a row -- to_real, to_cstring, then is_numeric_like/to_int_slow/rt_concat_parts_d -- and each leak
# was found the same way: by watching a program that worked yesterday stop working. Three asks in a row is
# the finding, not the arms (R-662). This file turns "the tag leaks and I find out later" into a census.
# ⛔ IT IS A DATA FILE ON PURPOSE, NOT A GREP. util_coercion_surface_census.py DISCOVERS every
# `switch (x.v)` / `switch (x->v)` under src/runtime and src/driver and REDS on any site not listed here --
# so the list cannot quietly fall behind the tree -- but WHICH TAGS a site owes is a human judgement that a
# grep cannot make, and it is recorded here where a reviewer can disagree with it.
#   tags_required is a comma-separated list of DT_* names that MUST appear inside that function's body.
#   `-` means the site is declared as covered-by-inspection and owes no specific tag (it is enumerated so
#   the discovery arm stays silent, and the `why` says who decided that and on what ground).
# ⭐ WHAT THIS CENSUS DOES NOT CLAIM. It proves a tag is MENTIONED in a site, never that the arm is correct.
# Correctness is the oracle's job. This is the cheap half that was missing entirely.
# ⛔ A SITE WHERE A BOOL MUST COERCE DIFFERENTLY FROM ITS 1/0 INTEGER VALUE IS AN ASK, NOT AN ARM
# (R-662's one standing exception). Such sites carry OPEN-ASK in the `why` column and no DT_BOOL in
# tags_required, so the census stays green while the question is with the officer rather than silently answered.

column4: why
numeric coercion; a Bool contributes its 1/0 integer value (R-656)
integer twin of to_real; same 1/0 value (R-662)
THE descriptor->string coercion; renders True/False, the same rendering R-656 ruled for to_cstring and R-662 for rt_concat_parts_d
the type-name table; answers BOOL

the CONVERT builtin: it tests DT_S only to materialize a counted string view once at entry (rt_cstr_d, hq_snobol4 2026-09-25) and DT_SNUL to route the null string; every value it returns is produced by VARVAL_fn / to_int / to_real / rt_str_to_real / pat_lit / code, each declared above or below, so a new tag is covered by delegation and owes no arm here

the tracer spells a value for a trace line; its default arm hands the value to VARVAL_fn, so it is correct BY DELEGATION and owes no arm of its own -- declared as a delegation rather than given a redundant case
DIFFER compares by value; a Bool differs from a value exactly as its 1/0 does
concatenation renders True/False (R-662)
sort orders by type rank first; an unranked tag sorts arbitrarily against every other
method-dispatch string coercion; renders True/False (R-656)
the name method dispatch reports for a receiver; answers Bool
the .raku rendering of one scalar for a typed Hash, Pair, List or Array element: Nil, Bool::True and Bool::False, a number as itself, anything else a quoted Str (hq_raku 2026-10-03)
a Set / Bag / Mix weight read as a double: an Int, a Num or a Bool (True is 1, False is 0), anything else weighs nothing (hq_raku 2026-10-07)

a Pascal array or record element reference: it tests the base for an array block and answers a name-reference to the element cell, else hands the base to pas_arr_get's string element and parks the value in the caller's temporary; DT_BOOL is minted by the Raku lowering alone and a Pascal base is never a Bool, so it owes no arm of its own (hq_pascal 2026-10-09)
IDENT compares by value; a Bool is identical exactly as its 1/0 is
OPEN-ASK: the hash half of the same question; it must hash whatever tbl_key_str keys on, so it is ruled with it, never separately
OPEN-ASK: the equality half of the same question; same ruling, same reason

the IF-CHAIN descriptor->string coercion, and the one the `~` operator actually reaches (str_concat_d -> descr_to_str). It fell to FAILDESCR, which is why "x" ~ $bool rendered as "x": THE SITE THE SWITCH-ONLY DISCOVERY MISSED
an independent descriptor->string coercion with its own DT_I/DT_R arms; it does NOT delegate to c_VARVAL_fn, so it owes its own True/False
concatenation hands every non-DT_S/non-DT_DATA operand to descr_to_str; covered by delegation
string repetition stringifies its left operand through descr_to_str; covered by delegation
all arithmetic gates on is_numeric_like and then coerces with to_real/to_int, each of which carries the tag; covered by delegation

SNOBOL4 affirmation (R-1648): a string is read by SPITBOL's grammar (sno_numeric_operand), every other tag is gated by is_numeric_like, then to_real/to_int coerce, each carrying the tag; covered by delegation
the gate every arithmetic operation passes through; without the tag here rt_num_arith_body returns FAILDESCR and Bool arithmetic yields nothing (R-662)
Icon's `||` only: it rejects any operand failing core_icn_str_ok before coercing, and no Icon program can hold a Bool -- DT_BOOL is minted by the Raku lowering alone
routes only bignum-shaped operands; a Bool is a 1/0 machine integer and is never a big
cset complement; a Bool is not a cset and FAILDESCR is the right answer
Icon's `*x`; unreachable from Raku, which is the only frontend that mints DT_BOOL
subscripting; a Bool is not a container and FAILDESCR is the right answer
two-dimensional subscripting; same reason as subscript_get_s
subscripting a variable; same reason
subscripting restricted to containers; a Bool is explicitly not one
dereferences a name; a Bool is a value, never a name
assignment target resolution; a Bool is never an lvalue

the s[i:j] variable; tests the base for a string that is not a cset (a subscripted cset is a value, hq_icon 2026-09-24), and a Bool is neither, so it takes the value path with FAILDESCR-or-value as before

the :=: swap; its one-character fast path tests the base cell for a string that is not a cset (hq_icon 2026-09-24) and hands every other value to the two-assignment path, so a Bool is never coerced here
list-bang over a container; a Bool is not one
random selection from a container; a Bool is not one
EVAL of a string or expression value; a Bool is neither
calls a value as a function; a Bool is not callable
generator half of rt_call_value; same reason
Prolog is/2 arithmetic, the cold evaluator behind the R7 inline arm (rt_pl_dop_is_v_c until 2026-09-26); Prolog cannot hold a DT_BOOL
Prolog's ISO number test behind number_codes/number_chars (DT_I, DT_R, DT_BIG); Prolog cannot hold a DT_BOOL (hq_prolog 2026-09-24)
Prolog term comparison fast path; same reason
SNOBOL4 &RANDOM setter; unreachable from Raku
SNOBOL4 &ERROR setter; unreachable from Raku
SNOBOL4 &TRACE setter; unreachable from Raku
SNOBOL4 &DUMP setter; unreachable from Raku

⭐ THE SITE THAT PROVES THE NAMING IS NOT A GUIDE: an `icn_`-prefixed gate that Raku's `eq`/`ne`/`lt` REACH. Without the tag, `$bool eq "True"` dies with error 103 "string expected" -- a live defect shipped in the previous landing, which this census found and the switch-only discovery could not (it returns a 0/1 verdict, not FAILDESCR)
the chars-family twin of core_icn_str_ok, carried for the same reason: a Bool has a string value, and the previous site is standing proof that an icn_ name does not mean Icon-only
cset operands only; Rakudo has no cset and a Bool is correctly rejected
Icon's explicit conversion gate; unreachable from the one frontend that mints DT_BOOL
Prolog unbound-variable test; Prolog cannot hold a DT_BOOL
Prolog unbound tag test; same reason
Prolog ISO unbound-variable test; Prolog cannot hold a DT_BOOL
Prolog text balance check; same reason
Prolog atomic_list_concat/2,3; same reason
Prolog atom_concat/3; same reason

SCRIP_GC_MAPS reporter only, never a coercion: it asks whether a tag REFERENCES THE HEAP, not what a value coerces to, and it is read-only beside the conservative scan. A new tag owes a row here only if the tag can hold a heap pointer; a new non-referencing tag correctly falls to default and is counted as not-a-slot (F6 step 3, R-867)

SCRIP_GC_MAPS frame walker-reporter only, never a coercion (cto 2026-09-19, CTO-88): it asks whether a byte in a DESCR-kinded frame slot is a known tag at all, so residue in an unzeroed slot is counted (i_badtag) instead of guessed at; a new tag owes a row here because the walker must know it exists.

SCRIP_GC_MAPS frame walker-reporter only, never a coercion (cto 2026-09-19, CTO-88): the pointer-bearing tags gc_visit_one visits, used to tell a tagged spine cell from a raw word beside it; a new tag owes a row here only if the tag can hold a heap pointer, exactly as gc_type_says_ref above.

SORT/RSORT arguments: the first must be an array or table (256), a vector's second must convert to a field name (257) -- a Bool is not a name, so 257 is its right answer; the column goes through rt_sno_cnv_num (258)

Icon loadfunc only: it reads the iconx descriptor word a loaded C function returned (ICNX_D_Integer/Real/Lrgint/External or a string length) and mints the SCRIP value; it switches on no SCRIP tag, so a new SCRIP tag owes no arm here (hq_icon 2026-09-28, external values)

Raku ~~: the range arm answers a DT_BOOL itself and the subject is stringified by to_cstring, which owes and has its own DT_BOOL arm (declared above); classified by vice_president 2026-11-06, fleet-preflight coercion census

Raku .ord: an array subject is joined, a Num is rendered by rk_real_str and every other receiver, a Bool included, is stringified by to_cstring (True/False), so True.ord is the code point of T by DELEGATION and the site owes no arm of its own
Raku .subst: the :g adverb arrives as a DT_BOOL argument and is read by an arm of its own, and the subject is stringified by to_cstring (DT_BOOL arm declared above)

DEFECT, NOT A CLASSIFICATION (fleet-preflight coercion census, vice_president 2026-11-06, MEASURED on SCRIP 88686b571 built fresh): div and mod coerce an operand that is not an Int or a Num by to_cstring then strtod, so a Bool becomes the text True and reads as 0.0; `7 div True` and `7 mod True` and `9 % True` print Failure where Rakudo prints 7, 0 and 0 (a Bool is its 1/0 integer, R-656; `2 + True` and `True * 5` are right because to_real has the arm). It owes a DT_BOOL arm (1/0) exactly as to_real; the arm stays RED here until the Raku designer's row lands it

Icon display(depth, file): the depth is coerced by to_int (which owes and has its DT_BOOL arm) after a null test (DT_SNUL means the default depth), the file by a handle or integer test, and DT_S only guards the image text it prints; Icon only, and DT_BOOL is minted by the Raku builtins alone

Raku push/append/prepend/unshift: the Int/Num test chooses Rakudo's Cannot resolve caller diagnostic for an immutable number receiver and every other receiver is listified by rk_av, so the tag test converts no value
the Prolog read_term parser: its if-chains test LEXER TOKEN kinds (GT_VAR, GT_INT, GT_FLOAT, GT_STR, GT_NAME, GT_BQ, GT_IOPEN, GT_PUNCT), never a descriptor tag; there is no descriptor to coerce
Prolog: the number test (integer, big integer, float) of the standard-order sort; a Prolog term never carries a DT_BOOL (minted by the Raku builtins alone, as pas_elem_ref records)
Prolog abolish/1: the predicate indicator is read from a DT_PLREF functor or a DT_PLATOM / DT_S atom and anything else FAILs; the tag test selects the predicate, it coerces no value; Prolog only

SNOBOL4 by-name call check: DT_N (a returned name) and DT_S (the called function's name) are read, no value is coerced; a value returned to a by-name call other than EVAL and ITEM is error 21, and DT_BOOL is not a SNOBOL4 value
SNOBOL4 container check: DT_A, DT_T and DATA instances are the containers that take the error code; any other value is returned unchanged (`return r`), so a Bool passes through as itself
SNOBOL4 ARRAY(dimensions, init): a numeric first argument by rt_num_arg_d, else a DT_S prototype string (rt_cstr_d), else error 64; the init value is stored as given; SNOBOL4 only
SNOBOL4 COPY: arrays, data instances, tables, patterns (DT_P), expressions (DT_X) and code (DT_C) are copied; every other value ends at `return v`, so a Bool copies to the same Bool
Icon getpw(): a null or absent argument reads the next entry, a DT_I is a uid, a DT_S a user name, any other tag FAILs; no value is coerced; Icon only
Icon getgr(): a null or absent argument reads the next entry, a DT_I is a gid, a DT_S a group name, any other tag FAILs; no value is coerced; Icon only
Icon getserv(): a name (DT_S) or a port (DT_I) selects the service entry, a null argument reads the next, any other tag FAILs; no value is coerced; Icon only
Icon process-argument formatter: a string (not a cset) is its text, an integer its decimal form, anything else NULL and the caller refuses it; Icon only
SNOBOL4 NRETURN: a DT_N stays a name; a DT_S, DT_I or DT_R is turned into a name by c_rt_sno_name_dl; anything else is error 243 function result in nreturn is not name; SNOBOL4 only

Unicon list(x): a set (DT_T with is_set) or a list (DT_DATA) argument makes a new list of its members; the tag selects the container to copy, the members are copied as they are; no value is coerced; Icon and Unicon only
Unicon socket subscripted by an attribute name: the name is a DT_S or null, any other tag FAILs; the answer is the attribute or a table of them; no value is coerced; Icon and Unicon only

Unicon receive: a co-expression (DT_CO) or null names the sender, a list is the queue to take from, any other tag FAILs; the message is returned as it was sent; no value is coerced; Icon and Unicon only
